nodes.label: Checkpoint B Hard Stop
nodes.rationale: No VM may start until the readiness report and watchdog are reviewed and a maximum 60-minute Checkpoint B window is explicitly authorized.

nodes.label: Graphify-First Repository Navigation
nodes.rationale: Scoped graph queries reduce broad source browsing and preserve a current architecture map.

nodes.label: Infrastructure Security and Cost Controls
nodes.rationale: Secrets and state artifacts stay untracked, and cost-heavy DNS Private Resolver resources require explicit approval.

nodes.label: Offline Reconciler Test Boundary
nodes.rationale: Tests must not depend on network access, cloud credentials, or Azure login.

nodes.label: Three-Layer Skill Routing
nodes.rationale: Choose process, then the smallest domain specialist set, then repository tools and facts so ownership is settled before evidence gathering.

nodes.label: Repository Evidence Order
nodes.rationale: Existing graph queries and focused project artifacts precede broad search; external facts use current official sources.

nodes.label: Mechanical Change Orchestration Bypass
nodes.rationale: Only a single-file, non-behavioral, non-security, non-architecture change may bypass orchestration, and it still receives a proportionate check.

nodes.label: Unavailable Skill and Check Fallback
nodes.rationale: Missing skills and checks are reported and replaced with the closest safe evidence path; they are never fabricated.

nodes.label: Three-Layer Operating Model
nodes.rationale: Process owns workflow, domain specialists refine execution, and repository tools supply evidence and actions.

nodes.label: Hybrid Enforcement Policy
nodes.rationale: Routing is mandatory for ambiguity, failures, security work, reviews, audits, and completion verification, while truly mechanical edits may use a bounded bypass.

nodes.label: Process Conflict Boundaries
nodes.rationale: An active GSD lifecycle owns plans and gates; Superpowers planning workflows cannot be nested into the same phase.
